claim: Synaptotagmin-1 and synaptotagmin-7 act as standalone fast and slow Ca2+-sensors for vesicle fusion in mouse chromaffin cells when present alone.
source: We find that synaptotagmin-1 and synaptotagmin-7 when present alone act as standalone fast and slow Ca2+-sensors for vesicle fusion in mouse chromaffin cells.
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1, where Syt-1 and Syt-7 were individually expressed in double knockout cells and shown to support fast and slow release, respectively.

claim: When present together, synaptotagmin-1 and synaptotagmin-7 are found in largely non-overlapping clusters on dense-core vesicles.
source: When present together, synaptotagmin-1 and synaptotagmin-7 are found in largely non-overlapping clusters on dense-core vesicles.
evidence: This claim is stated in the abstract and supported by 3D-SIM imaging data in Figure 9, showing that only 7.0 ± 0.4% of Syt-1-positive structures colocalized with Syt-7, and 4.1 ± 0.6% of Syt-7-positive structures colocalized with Syt-1.

claim: Synaptotagmin-7 stimulates Ca2+-dependent vesicle priming.
source: Synaptotagmin-7 stimulates Ca2+-dependent vesicle priming and inhibits depriming
evidence: This claim is stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figures 2 and 3, showing that Ca2+-dependent priming was almost absent in Syt-7 KO cells and enhanced by Syt-7 overexpression.

claim: Synaptotagmin-7 inhibits depriming.
source: Synaptotagmin-7 stimulates Ca2+-dependent vesicle priming and inhibits depriming
evidence: This claim is stated in the abstract and supported by recovery experiments in Figure 4, showing that the depriming rate (k-1) was significantly higher in the Syt-7 KO than in WT cells.

claim: Synaptotagmin-7 promotes ubMunc13-2-dependent priming.
source: it promotes ubMunc13-2- and phorbolester-dependent priming, especially at low resting calcium concentrations
evidence: This claim is stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 7, showing that ubMunc13-2 overexpression increased RRP size more in Syt-7 WT than in Syt-7 KO cells.

claim: Synaptotagmin-7 promotes phorbolester-dependent priming, especially at low resting calcium concentrations.
source: it promotes ubMunc13-2- and phorbolester-dependent priming, especially at low resting calcium concentrations
evidence: This claim is stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 6, showing that PMA caused a robust increase in secretion in WT cells but only a minor potentiation in Syt-7 KO cells when stimulated from low prestimulation [Ca2+].

claim: The priming effect of synaptotagmin-7 increases the number of vesicles fusing via synaptotagmin-1.
source: The priming effect of synaptotagmin-7 increases the number of vesicles fusing via synaptotagmin-1, while negatively affecting their fusion speed
evidence: This claim is stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 2G showing that Syt-7 increases RRP size (which depends on Syt-1 for fusion).

claim: Synaptotagmin-7 negatively affects the fusion speed of vesicles fusing via synaptotagmin-1.
source: The priming effect of synaptotagmin-7 increases the number of vesicles fusing via synaptotagmin-1, while negatively affecting their fusion speed
evidence: This claim is stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 2H showing that fusion kinetics were sped up by Syt-7 knockout and slowed down upon reexpression.

claim: Synaptotagmin-7 places vesicles in close membrane apposition (<6 nm).
source: Synaptotagmin-7 places vesicles in close membrane apposition (<6 nm); without it, vesicles accumulate out of reach of the fusion complex (20–40 nm).
evidence: This claim is stated in the abstract and supported by electron tomography data in Figure 8P,T showing that the number of vesicles within 0-6 nm of the plasma membrane was significantly reduced in the Syt-7 KO.

claim: Without synaptotagmin-7, vesicles accumulate out of reach of the fusion complex (20–40 nm).
source: Synaptotagmin-7 places vesicles in close membrane apposition (<6 nm); without it, vesicles accumulate out of reach of the fusion complex (20–40 nm).
evidence: This claim is stated in the abstract and supported by electron tomography data in Figure 8P showing an increased number of vesicles at 20-40 nm from the plasma membrane in the Syt-7 KO.

claim: Syt-1 supports a small rapid burst of secretion with a fusion time constant around 10–20 ms.
source: Syt-1 supported a small rapid burst of secretion, with a fusion time constant around 10–20 ms (Figure 1A–C).
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by capacitance measurements shown in Figure 1A-C.

claim: Syt-7 stimulates a larger burst of secretion with a much slower fusion time constant, around 500 ms.
source: In contrast, Syt-7 stimulated a larger burst of secretion, but with a much slower fusion time constant, around 500 ms (Figure 1A–C).
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by capacitance measurements shown in Figure 1A-C.

claim: Syt-1 supported fast secretion (i.e. an RRP, fusion time constant 13.4 ± 1.47 ms), but not slow-burst secretion (i.e. an SRP).
source: Syt-1 supported fast secretion (i.e. an RRP, fusion time constant 13.4 ± 1.47 ms), but not slow-burst secretion (i.e. an SRP)
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by kinetic analysis shown in Figure 1B-C.

claim: Syt-7 only supported slow secretion (SRP fusion time constant: 500 ± 48.9 ms).
source: whereas Syt-7 only supported slow secretion (SRP fusion time constant: 500 ± 48.9 ms; Figure 1B–C).
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by kinetic analysis shown in Figure 1B-C.

claim: The slow burst became faster in the presence of Syt-1.
source: The data also show that the slow burst became faster in the presence of Syt-1, and the fast burst was slower in the presence of Syt-7 (Figure 1C)
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 1C showing changes in fusion kinetics.

claim: The fast burst was slower in the presence of Syt-7.
source: The data also show that the slow burst became faster in the presence of Syt-1, and the fast burst was slower in the presence of Syt-7 (Figure 1C)
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 1C showing changes in fusion kinetics.

claim: Expression of either Syt-1 or Syt-7 can re-establish release in Syt-1/7 DKO cells.
source: Thus, expression of either Syt-1 or Syt-7 can re-establish release in Syt-1/7 DKO cells and Syt-1 triggers faster fusion than Syt-7.
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 1A showing that both Syt-1 and Syt-7 expression rescued secretion in DKO cells.

claim: Syt-1 triggers faster fusion than Syt-7.
source: Thus, expression of either Syt-1 or Syt-7 can re-establish release in Syt-1/7 DKO cells and Syt-1 triggers faster fusion than Syt-7.
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 1 showing faster kinetics for Syt-1-driven release compared to Syt-7.

claim: Expression of either Syt-1 or Syt-7 increased the spike frequency in DKO cells.
source: Expression of either Syt-1 or Syt-7 increased the spike frequency – or, equivalently, reduced the spike interval (Figure 1E,G).
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by amperometry data in Figure 1E,G.

claim: Syt-1 caused a shorter spike duration than Syt-7.
source: When analyzing the shape of the amperometric spikes, Syt-1 caused a shorter spike duration than Syt-7 (Figure 1H)
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by amperometry data in Figure 1H.

claim: Syt-1 caused a faster half-life than Syt-7.
source: a faster half-life (Figure 1I)
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by amperometry data in Figure 1I.

claim: Syt-1 caused a faster rise time than Syt-7.
source: a faster rise time (Figure 1L)
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by amperometry data in Figure 1L.

claim: Syt-1 caused a faster decay time than Syt-7.
source: a faster decay time (Figure 1M)
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by amperometry data in Figure 1M.

claim: Syt-1 caused a shorter duration of the 'foot' signal than Syt-7.
source: and a shorter duration of the so-called 'foot' signal (Figure 1N).
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by amperometry data in Figure 1N.

claim: The foot signal measures the duration of the fusion pore prior to pore expansion.
source: The foot signal measures the duration of the fusion pore prior to pore expansion (Chow et al., 1992).
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: A longer foot signal following overexpression of Syt-7 compared to Syt-1 was previously found in PC12-cells.
source: A longer foot signal following overexpression of Syt-7 compared to Syt-1 was previously found in PC12-cells (Zhang et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Optical means (TIRF-microscopy) showed a longer duration of the exocytotic event driven by Syt-7.
source: These findings agree with and expand on data obtained using optical means (TIRF-microscopy), which showed a longer duration of the exocytotic event driven by Syt-7 (Bendahmane et al., 2020; Rao et al., 2014; Rao et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: With Syt-7 overexpression, spike kinetics was indistinguishable from the Syt-1/7 DKO condition.
source: Notably, with Syt-7 overexpression, spike kinetics was indistinguishable from the Syt-1/7 DKO condition.
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by amperometry data in Figure 1.

claim: Knockout of Syt-7 caused a decrease in secretion as measured by both capacitance and amperometry when stimulated from low prestimulation [Ca2+].
source: Under these conditions, knockout of Syt-7 caused a decrease in secretion as measured by both capacitance and amperometry (Figure 2A,E; Figure 2—figure supplement 1A)
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 2A,E and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Re-expression of Syt-7 caused rescue of secretion to WT levels when stimulated from low prestimulation [Ca2+].
source: whereas re-expression of Syt-7 caused rescue of secretion to WT levels (Figure 2A,E).
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 2A,E.

claim: Lentiviral expression of WT Syt-7 results in levels ~ twofold higher than endogenous Syt-7.
source: Expression analysis by immunofluorescence showed that lentiviral expression of the WT Syt-7 results in levels ~ twofold higher than endogenous Syt-7 (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A–B).
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A–B.

claim: At high prestimulation [Ca2+] (~0.8 µM), Syt-7 expressing cells displayed markedly more burst-like secretion.
source: Under these conditions, Syt-7 expressing cells displayed markedly more burst-like secretion (Figure 2F,J), consistent with Ca2+-dependent vesicle priming.
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 2F,J.

claim: Both fast (RRP) and slow (SRP) burst secretion were strongly and significantly decreased by Syt-7 knockout and rescued by Syt-7 expression at high prestimulation [Ca2+].
source: Both fast (RRP) and slow (SRP) burst secretion were strongly and significantly decreased by Syt-7 knockout and rescued by Syt-7 expression (Figure 2G).
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 2G.

claim: The kinetics of fusion from the RRP and SRP were sped up by Syt-7 knockout, and this was rescued upon reexpression.
source: The kinetics of fusion from the RRP and SRP were sped up by Syt-7 knockout, and this was also rescued upon reexpression (Figure 2H).
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 2H.

claim: The sustained rate was reduced in the Syt-7 KO, but this aspect was not rescued upon overexpression at high prestimulation [Ca2+].
source: Curiously, the sustained rate was reduced in the Syt-7 KO, but this aspect was not rescued upon overexpression (Figure 2I).
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 2I.

claim: RRP and SRP sizes in the KO + Syt-7 condition were even higher than in Syt-7 WT cells at high prestimulation [Ca2+].
source: However, RRP and SRP sizes in the KO + Syt-7 condition were even higher than in Syt-7 WT cells, leading to an overshoot in overall secretion within the first second after stimulation (Figure 2F,G).
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 2F,G.

claim: Almost all fast secretion from the RRP in chromaffin cells depends on Syt-1.
source: Almost all fast secretion from the RRP in chromaffin cells depends on Syt-1 (Nagy et al., 2006; Voets et al., 2001) (see also Figure 1).
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by citations to previous work and data in Figure 1.

claim: The data showing potentiation of the RRP size by Syt-7 indicates a cooperative/competitive interplay between Syt-7 and Syt-1.
source: Therefore, the data showing potentiation of the RRP size by Syt-7 indicates a cooperative/competitive interplay between Syt-7 and Syt-1, such that Syt-7 increases the amplitude of Syt-1 driven exocytosis (cooperation, Figure 2G), but slows down its fusion kinetics (competition, Figure 2H)
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 2G,H showing that Syt-7 increases RRP size but slows fusion kinetics.

claim: The main Ca2+-dependent priming step in chromaffin cells is located upstream of the SRP.
source: The main Ca2+-dependent priming step is in chromaffin cells located upstream of the SRP, which in turn is connected to the RRP (Voets, 2000).
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: By acting at the upstream priming step ('priming I'), Syt-7 regulates both SRP and RRP size.
source: By acting at the upstream priming step ('priming I', Houy et al., 2017), Syt-7 regulates both SRP and RRP size.
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by a citation and data showing effects on both SRP and RRP.

claim: At higher calcium concentrations (>0.5 µM), the burst size decreases because the high prestimulation calcium causes some release before the flash.
source: at higher calcium concentrations the burst size decreases because the high prestimulation calcium causes some release before the flash (Figure 3; Voets, 2000), thereby reducing the releasable pool sizes.
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 3 and a citation to previous work.

claim: Ca2+-dependent priming was almost absent in Syt-7 KO cells.
source: Strikingly, Ca2+-dependent priming was almost absent in Syt-7 KO cells (Figure 3).
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 3.

claim: Expression of Syt-7 in KO cells enhanced priming beyond WT levels at [Ca2+] above 0.2 µM.
source: In contrast, expression of Syt-7 in KO cells enhanced priming beyond WT levels at [Ca2+] above 0.2 µM (Figure 3).
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 3.

claim: The RRP was significantly increased in the Syt-7 KO when comparing low vs high prestimulation [Ca2+].
source: Further analysis of this showed that the RRP was significantly increased in the Syt-7 KO (low prestimulation [Ca2+], RRP size: 16.7 ± 3.10 fF; high prestimulation [Ca2+], RRP size: 29.1 ± 4.08 fF. p=0.0480, Mann Whitney test)
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by statistical analysis of data.

claim: Syt-7 is necessary for strong Ca2+-dependent priming in adrenal chromaffin cells.
source: Thus, Syt-7 is necessary for strong Ca2+-dependent priming in adrenal chromaffin cells, and overexpressing the protein further boosts this function
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 3 showing reduced priming in Syt-7 KO.

claim: Overexpressing Syt-7 further boosts Ca2+-dependent priming.
source: Thus, Syt-7 is necessary for strong Ca2+-dependent priming in adrenal chromaffin cells, and overexpressing the protein further boosts this function
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 3 showing enhanced priming with Syt-7 overexpression.

claim: In Syt-7 KO cells, a small Ca2+-dependent priming effect persists.
source: in Syt-7 KO cells, a small Ca2+-dependent priming effect persists.
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by data showing a slight increase in RRP size with higher prestimulation [Ca2+] in Syt-7 KO.

claim: All three mutations (C2A*, C2B*, C2AB*) in Syt-7 failed to rescue the increase in RRP and SRP size.
source: Using Ca2+ uncaging we found that all three mutations (C2A*, C2B*, C2AB*) failed to rescue the increase in RRP and SRP size (Figure 2—figure supplement 2C–F).
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 2—figure supplement 2C–F.

claim: The C2 domains of Syt-7 act synergistically in binding to PI(4,5)P2-containing membranes.
source: However, our findings agree with a recent report that the C2 domains of Syt-7 act synergistically in binding to PI(4,5)P2-containing membranes (Tran et al., 2019)
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: The Ca2+-binding sites in the C2B-domain are critical for Syt-7 function in chromaffin cells.
source: and previous data obtained from knockin (C2B-mutated) Syt-7 mice, which displayed a phenotype similar to Syt-7 KO in chromaffin cells (Schonn et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by a citation to previous work and data in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: The depriming rate (k-1) was significantly higher in the Syt-7 KO whether the 60 ms or the 600 ms time point was considered.
source: This rate was significantly higher in the Syt-7 KO whether the 60 ms or the 600 ms time point was considered (Figure 4B–C, Table 1).
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 4B–C and Table 1.

claim: The forward priming rate ([Depot] ∙ k1) was similar for Syt-7 KO and WT at 60 ms.
source: Together with the different steady-state pool sizes, this allows us to calculate the forward priming rate, i.e. [Depot] ∙ k1, which was similar for Syt-7 KO and WT at 60 ms (WT: 3.21 ± 0.63 fF/s, Syt-7 KO: 3.07 ± 0.95 fF/s; Table 1)
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by data in Table 1.

claim: The forward priming rate was higher for the Syt-7 KO than the WT at the 600 ms time point.
source: and even higher for the Syt-7 KO than the WT at the 600 ms time point (WT: 8.60 ± 1.12 fF/s, Syt-7 KO: 15.8 ± 3.32 fF/s; Table 1).
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by data in Table 1.

claim: In the WT, the priming rate increases slightly after stimulation.
source: Accordingly, in the WT the priming rate increases slightly after stimulation
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by data in Table 1 showing increased k1*DP after stimulation in WT.

claim: In the Syt-7 KO, the priming rate drops following stimulation.
source: however, in the Syt-7 KO the priming rate drops following stimulation (WT at 60 ms: 3.21 ± 0.63 fF/s before and 3.78 ± 0.78 fF/s after stimulation, Syt-7 KO at 60 ms: 3.07 ± 0.95 fF/s before and 1.90 ± 0.62 fF/s after secretion, Table 1).
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by data in Table 1 showing decreased k1*DP after stimulation in Syt-7 KO.

claim: k1 increases in the Syt-7 WT after stimulation.
source: We conclude that k1 increases in the Syt-7 WT after stimulation, whereas in the Syt-7 KO this increase is absent or insufficient, leading to incomplete recovery.
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by analysis of recovery data and priming rates in Table 1.

claim: In the Syt-7 KO, the increase in k1 after stimulation is absent or insufficient, leading to incomplete recovery.
source: We conclude that k1 increases in the Syt-7 WT after stimulation, whereas in the Syt-7 KO this increase is absent or insufficient, leading to incomplete recovery.
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by analysis of recovery data and priming rates in Table 1.

claim: NEM led to an increase in the burst and total amount of release in the Syt-7 KO when stimulated from low prestimulation [Ca2+].
source: Strikingly, this led to an increase in the burst and total amount of release in the Syt-7 KO (Figure 5A–D).
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 5A–D.

claim: In the presence of NEM, secretion in the Syt-7 KO became indistinguishable from WT when stimulated from low prestimulation [Ca2+].
source: Indeed, in the presence of NEM, secretion in the Syt-7 KO became indistinguishable from WT, whereas in WT cells, NEM was without significant effect (Figure 5A–D).
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 5A–D.

claim: In WT cells, NEM was without significant effect when stimulated from low prestimulation [Ca2+].
source: Indeed, in the presence of NEM, secretion in the Syt-7 KO became indistinguishable from WT, whereas in WT cells, NEM was without significant effect (Figure 5A–D).
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 5A–D.

claim: NEM specifically increased RRP size when stimulated from low prestimulation [Ca2+].
source: Kinetic analysis showed that NEM specifically increased RRP size (Figure 5E), but with no significant effect on SRP size (Figure 5G) or on the fast or slow time constants of release.
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 5E.

claim: NEM had no significant effect on SRP size when stimulated from low prestimulation [Ca2+].
source: Kinetic analysis showed that NEM specifically increased RRP size (Figure 5E), but with no significant effect on SRP size (Figure 5G) or on the fast or slow time constants of release.
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 5G.

claim: No effect of NEM was found in the Syt-7 WT when stimulated from low prestimulation [Ca2+].
source: Since no effect of NEM was found in the Syt-7 WT, the effect of NEM is occluded by Syt-7 expression.
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 5.

claim: The effect of NEM is occluded by Syt-7 expression.
source: Since no effect of NEM was found in the Syt-7 WT, the effect of NEM is occluded by Syt-7 expression.
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 5 showing no effect of NEM in WT but an effect in Syt-7 KO.

claim: Syt-7 acts to protect SNARE-complexes from disassembly.
source: This finding is consistent with a function of Syt-7 to protect SNARE-complexes from disassembly, which probably underlies the function of Syt-7 to decrease the depriming rate.
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by data showing that NEM rescues priming in Syt-7 KO but not in WT.

claim: In the Syt-7 KO, SNARE-complexes are left (partly) unprotected and priming can therefore be rescued by NEM.
source: In the Syt-7 KO, SNARE-complexes are left (partly) unprotected and priming can therefore be rescued by NEM, whereas in the Syt-7 WT, where SNARE-complexes are already protected, NEM has no effect.
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by data showing differential effects of NEM in Syt-7 KO vs WT.

claim: In the Syt-7 WT, where SNARE-complexes are already protected, NEM has no effect.
source: In the Syt-7 KO, SNARE-complexes are left (partly) unprotected and priming can therefore be rescued by NEM, whereas in the Syt-7 WT, where SNARE-complexes are already protected, NEM has no effect.
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by data showing no effect of NEM in Syt-7 WT.

claim: The main Munc13-protein in chromaffin cells is ubMunc13-2.
source: The main Munc13-protein in chromaffin cells, ubMunc13-2, acts at the same upstream priming step (priming I) (Man et al., 2015), as Syt-7 (see above).
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: ubMunc13-2 acts at the same upstream priming step (priming I) as Syt-7.
source: The main Munc13-protein in chromaffin cells, ubMunc13-2, acts at the same upstream priming step (priming I) (Man et al., 2015), as Syt-7 (see above).
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by a citation to previous work and data showing effects on the same pools.

claim: Munc13-2 overexpression is the strongest known manipulation to increase the primed LDCV pool in chromaffin cells.
source: Munc13-2 overexpression is the strongest known manipulation to increase the primed LDCV pool in chromaffin cells (Zikich et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Secretion is potentiated by phorbolesters.
source: Secretion is also potentiated by phorbolesters (Smith et al., 1998), which activate Munc13-proteins and Protein Kinase C (Rhee et al., 2002; Wierda et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Phorbolesters activate Munc13-proteins and Protein Kinase C.
source: Secretion is also potentiated by phorbolesters (Smith et al., 1998), which activate Munc13-proteins and Protein Kinase C (Rhee et al., 2002; Wierda et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: In chromaffin cells, the effect of phorbolesters includes a potentiation of the upstream priming step, leading to a larger exocytotic burst.
source: In chromaffin cells, the effect includes a potentiation of the upstream priming step, leading to a larger exocytotic burst (Smith et al., 1998).
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: PMA caused a robust increase in secretion in WT cells when stimulated from low prestimulation [Ca2+], resulting from an increase in SRP and RRP size.
source: Under these circumstances, PMA caused a robust increase in secretion in WT cells, resulting from an increase in SRP and RRP size, but not of the sustained component (overall secretion increased by 126%; Figure 6A–D).
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 6A–D.

claim: PMA did not increase the sustained component in WT cells when stimulated from low prestimulation [Ca2+].
source: Under these circumstances, PMA caused a robust increase in secretion in WT cells, resulting from an increase in SRP and RRP size, but not of the sustained component (overall secretion increased by 126%; Figure 6A–D).
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 6A–D.

claim: Overall secretion increased by 126% with PMA in WT cells when stimulated from low prestimulation [Ca2+].
source: Under these circumstances, PMA caused a robust increase in secretion in WT cells, resulting from an increase in SRP and RRP size, but not of the sustained component (overall secretion increased by 126%; Figure 6A–D).
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 6A–D.

claim: PMA led to faster SRP secretion in WT cells when stimulated from low prestimulation [Ca2+].
source: PMA further led to faster SRP secretion (Figure 6C), whereas RRP secretion kinetics were not affected.
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 6C.

claim: RRP secretion kinetics were not affected by PMA in WT cells when stimulated from low prestimulation [Ca2+].
source: PMA further led to faster SRP secretion (Figure 6C), whereas RRP secretion kinetics were not affected.
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 6C.

claim: In Syt-7 KO cells, PMA resulted in only a minor potentiation of overall release (21%) when stimulated from low prestimulation [Ca2+].
source: However, in Syt-7 KO cells, the situation was different: PMA resulted in only a minor potentiation of overall release (21%, Figure 6E–H)
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 6E–H.

claim: PMA resulted in a small increase in RRP (which was statistically significant) in Syt-7 KO cells when stimulated from low prestimulation [Ca2+].
source: due to a small increase in RRP (which was statistically significant) and SRP size (p=0.0506; Figure 6F).
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 6F.

claim: Syt-7 is necessary for PMA to exert its full priming effect at low prestimulation [Ca2+].
source: Thus, Syt-7 is necessary for PMA to exert its full priming effect at low prestimulation [Ca2+] (data on higher prestimulation [Ca2+] are presented below).
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 6 showing reduced PMA effect in Syt-7 KO.

claim: Overexpression of ubMunc13-2 in WT chromaffin cells resulted in massive secretion, which reached 1.0–1.5 pF when stimulated from low prestimulation [Ca2+].
source: Overexpression of ubMunc13-2 in WT chromaffin cells using a Semliki Forest Virus construct resulted in massive secretion, which reached 1.0–1.5 pF (Figure 7A; data from Syt-7 WT and KO are the same as in Figure 2) when again assayed from a low prestimulation [Ca2+]
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 7A.

claim: ubMunc13-2 overexpression caused a massive increase in both RRP and SRP sizes when stimulated from low prestimulation [Ca2+].
source: This was due to a massive increase in both RRP and SRP sizes (Figure 7D,G), as previously reported from bovine chromaffin cells (Zikich et al., 2008).
